question: Should Reef core own, release, and support the Node/PostgreSQL Kubernetes relay and its long-term compatibility contract alongside the Cloudflare relay?
rationale: This is a new persistent deployment platform with database, migration, Helm, SMTP, WebSocket, and upgrade responsibilities; the code can be reviewed, but only maintainers can choose the permanent product and support boundary.

options.title: Defer core inclusion pending sponsorship
options.body: Keep the PR open while a Reef owner explicitly sponsors the platform boundary and expected long-term support obligations.

options.title: Adopt a dual-relay contract
options.body: Approve the Node/PostgreSQL relay as a supported core adapter, contingent on resolving the proxy-chain defect and adding inspectable deployment proof.

options.title: Keep Reef Cloudflare-focused
options.body: Decline the new core adapter and pursue a separately owned deployment path if portability remains desired.

recommendation.title: Defer core inclusion pending sponsorship
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open while a Reef owner explicitly sponsors the platform boundary and expected long-term support obligations.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Reef design identifies Peter with the agreed product design that this PR expands.
